analysis.title: GS Klein - Liquidity snapshot 8 Oct 2026
key_insights: YTD US equity volumes are averaging a record 19B shares and $1T a day. Volumes are up 10% y/y through 3Q, but top-of-book liquidity is flat and the trading environment remains fragile.
Daily executed value has doubled since 2023, from $511B to $1,041B, while top-of-book liquidity fell 21% over the same period.

June had a volume spike that included the two busiest volume days ever, 33B shares on 6/18 and 32B shares on 6/26. Top-of-book liquidity that month fell 33% versus May and has since recovered to YTD highs.
Top-of-book depth is down 76% since 2017 while daily share volume has nearly tripled. Top-of-book liquidity has been stable at $11M a day over the last two years.
Even in the higher-volume regime, top-of-book depth still evaporates in stressed tapes, and is thinnest when it is needed most.
risk_factors: Thin top-of-book liquidity relative to record volumes makes the trading environment fragile, and depth drops in stressed tapes.
Volume spikes such as June 2026 can coincide with sharp falls in top-of-book depth.
vol_and_positioning: Top-of-book depth is $11M a day, down 76% since 2017, and has been stable at that level for two years. Depth thins sharply in stressed markets, as in June when it fell 33% versus May.
